proof_nl:
Let t = nr. Since n > 1 and 0 ≤ r < 1, we have 0 ≤ t < n.

Now m = ⌊t⌋. By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer and m ≤ t < m + 1.

Because t ≥ 0, the integer 0 satisfies 0 ≤ t. Since ⌊t⌋ is the greatest integer not exceeding t, it follows that m = ⌊t⌋ ≥ 0.

Also, from m ≤ t and t < n, we get m < n.

Therefore 0 ≤ m < n, as required.
solver_summary: Set t = nr. Then 0 ≤ t < n. Since m = floor(t), m is an integer with m ≤ t < m+1, hence m ≥ 0 and m < n.
